title: Why you should record/edit in 24-bit and export in 16-bit
text: Music. And the coarser your ruler, the bigger each error and the louder that hiss. Here's what that is actually worth. At 8-bits the hiss sits about 50 decibels below full volume. At 16-bits about a 100. And 100 decibels is roughly the gap between a whisper and a rock concert. So at 16-bits the hiss is already quieter than the room you are sitting in right now. You will never hear it. So why does 24 exist? Because while you are working, every edit rounds all over again. Turn something up and you turn its hiss up with it. 24-bit gives you room to absorb all of that. So record and edit in 24. Export in 16. Your listener gains nothing from more. Bit depth isn't quality. It's room to work in. Keep it while you edit, spend it when you ship. I'm Rohan Vijayakumar for Humanitarian's AI.
